outcome: composite maternal mortality and morbidity (including infectious and hemorrhagic morbidity)
cohort: The study included nulliparous individuals with singleton pregnancies delivered at term (>=37 weeks) with a BMI of >=40 kg/m^2 at delivery, excluding those with spontaneous labor, fetal malformations, and stillbirths.
finding: Among nulliparous individuals with class III obesity at term, the rates of composite maternal and neonatal morbidity did not significantly differ between those who underwent labor induction and those who had a cesarean delivery without labor.
mod_finding: No significant difference in short-term maternal and neonatal morbidity was found between labor induction and cesarean delivery without labor.
